terms.name: Access key
terms.definition: A single letter, usually shown underlined, that jumps straight to a menu or control once the access modifier is held.

terms.name: Address autocomplete
terms.definition: Replacing a set of address fields with one lookup that suggests full addresses after a few characters and fills the rest on selection.

terms.name: App silhouette
terms.definition: The recognisable outline of an app's chrome, which bars and panes it has and where they sit, used to classify one app's layout against another's.

terms.name: Autoplay
terms.definition: Playback that starts with no gesture from the reader, which browsers now allow only while the sound is off, so autoplay in practice means a silent moving picture.

terms.name: Bottom sheet
terms.definition: A surface anchored to the bottom edge that slides up over the content, often draggable between a peeked and an expanded height.

terms.name: Bypassing pattern
terms.definition: A scanning shape where readers deliberately skip the opening words of each line because every line in a list starts the same way.

terms.name: Character key shortcuts
terms.definition: Single letter shortcuts that fire without a modifier, which must be switchable off or remappable because speech input and screen readers trigger them by accident.

terms.name: Close button
terms.definition: The small dismiss control in the corner of a dialog, banner or panel, drawn as an X and named Close rather than X.

terms.name: Color space
terms.definition: A coordinate system for describing colour, where the choice of axes decides whether arithmetic like mixing or stepping a ramp matches what the eye sees.

terms.name: Complication
terms.definition: A slot on a watch face filled with one live figure from an app, sized to be read in the second a wrist is raised.

terms.name: Content shelf
terms.definition: A horizontally scrolling row of cards, one row per category, stacked down the page so each row is browsed sideways.

terms.name: Cursor follower
terms.definition: A dot or ring that trails the pointer with a lag and often swells over links, replacing or augmenting the native cursor as a piece of brand motion.

terms.name: Deformable UI
terms.definition: A style where controls behave like soft matter, squashing under a press and springing back past rest, so the surface reads as jelly, clay, or inflated plastic rather than paint.

terms.name: Disguised ad
terms.definition: An advertisement styled to look like a control or an item of content, so the click it collects was aimed at something else entirely.

terms.name: Drag to reorder
terms.definition: Changing the order of a list by dragging an item to a new position, with the remaining items shifting to show where it will land.

terms.name: Edge swipe
terms.definition: A swipe that begins off the screen edge and travels inward, reserved by the system for navigation such as going back or revealing a drawer.

terms.name: Error summary
terms.definition: A block at the top of a failed form listing every problem as links that move focus to the field that caused it.

terms.name: False bottom
terms.definition: A page that looks finished at a point where content actually continues, so the reader stops scrolling and never sees the rest.

terms.name: Flame graph
terms.definition: Stacked bars where width is time spent and depth is call nesting, so the widest plateau rather than the tallest tower is the thing worth fixing.

terms.name: Focus management
terms.definition: Deliberately moving keyboard focus after a state change so the reader lands on the new content instead of at the top of the document.

terms.name: Forced colors mode
terms.definition: An operating system mode that replaces a page's palette with a small user-chosen set of system colours, overriding almost everything an author specified.

terms.name: Glitch aesthetic
terms.definition: A look that fakes signal failure with colour channel offset, torn scan bands, and jitter, used for emphasis or as a whole visual identity.

terms.name: Gutter
terms.definition: The space between columns or tracks in a grid, distinct from the outer margin that separates the grid from the container edge.

terms.name: Hidden gesture
terms.definition: An action reachable only by an input the reader has to guess: a swipe, a long press, a two-finger tap, with nothing on screen saying it is there.

terms.name: Hyperreal 3D
terms.definition: Rendered objects pushed past photographic realism, with physically based materials, sharp specular detail, and studio lighting, floated over an otherwise plain interface.

terms.name: Inline autocomplete
terms.definition: Completing the reader's text inside the field itself, with the guessed remainder selected so the next keystroke replaces it.

terms.name: Isometric illustration
terms.definition: Art drawn on a fixed axonometric grid so depth reads without perspective, with parallel edges and no vanishing point.

terms.name: Keyline
terms.definition: An invisible line that content across a whole screen aligns to, such as the edge line every row starts at and the deeper line where text begins after an icon.

terms.name: Leaderboard
terms.definition: A ranked list of participants by some score, with the reader's own position pinned into view even when it falls outside the visible range.

terms.name: List detail
terms.definition: A browsable list paired with a pane showing the selected item in full, collapsing to one screen at a time when the window is narrow.

terms.name: Magnetic button
terms.definition: A control that leans toward the cursor as it approaches, translating a fraction of the distance to its centre so it reads as attracted rather than merely hovered.

terms.name: Mesh gradient
terms.definition: A soft multi-point blend built from colours placed on a grid and smoothed between them, giving the blurred, cloudlike backgrounds a linear gradient cannot.

terms.name: Modal presentation
terms.definition: The slide-up-over transition that puts a sheet or dialog in front of the current screen while what is behind recedes, the platform motion for entering a modal context.

terms.name: Multi-touch
terms.definition: Input from more than one simultaneous contact point, letting a surface distinguish two-finger scrolling, pinching, rotating and larger finger counts.

terms.name: No results state
terms.definition: What a search or filtered list shows when nothing matched, naming the query, explaining why, and offering a way to loosen the constraints.

terms.name: One-time code login
terms.definition: Signing in by typing a short code sent to a second channel, keeping the reader inside the app rather than sending them out to a mail client.

terms.name: Overscan safe area
terms.definition: The inset a television layout keeps clear of the screen edge, about five percent, because sets crop the outer frame and anything near it disappears.

terms.name: Particle background
terms.definition: An ambient decorative background of many small moving agents: drifting dots, linked constellations, flocks, or starfields animating behind the page content.

terms.name: Point size
terms.definition: The nominal size of type, measured in points, which describes the body the letters are drawn on rather than the height of any letter.

terms.name: Pressed state
terms.definition: The look a control takes while it is actually being held down, confirming that the press was received before the action runs.

terms.name: Proximity
terms.definition: The grouping principle that elements placed close together read as related, which is why spacing decides perceived structure more reliably than borders do.

terms.name: Range slider
terms.definition: A slider with two handles on one track that sets a lower and an upper bound, so the selection is an interval rather than a point.

terms.name: Relative timestamp
terms.definition: A time printed as a distance from now, two hours ago or in three days, updating itself and holding the exact time in its tooltip.

terms.name: Rotate gesture
terms.definition: Two fingers turning around a common center to rotate the object or view beneath them, the angle tracking the fingers as they orbit.

terms.name: Screen magnification
terms.definition: Blowing part of the screen up many times over, so a reader sees a keyhole of the layout at a time and anything far from the action is effectively off screen.

terms.name: Scrubby slider
terms.definition: A numeric field whose label can be dragged sideways to change the value, giving a slider's feel without a slider taking up room.

terms.name: Set size and position
terms.definition: Telling assistive technology how big a list really is and where an item sits in it, so a windowed or paginated list still announces "item 6 of 16".

terms.name: Slash command
terms.definition: Typing a forward slash in a composer to open a menu of actions, where choosing one runs it rather than inserting the words into the message.

terms.name: Sonification
terms.definition: Turning data into sound, mapping a series to pitch or rhythm, so a chart can be heard as a shape rather than described one value at a time.

terms.name: Spotted pattern
terms.definition: A scanning shape where the eye jumps to isolated words scattered down the page, hunting a keyword, a link or a number rather than reading anything.

terms.name: Stepper
terms.definition: A small two part control with minus and plus that nudges a number up or down one step at a time.

terms.name: Superscript
terms.definition: Small raised characters used for footnote markers, ordinals, and exponents, ideally drawn by the font rather than shrunk by software.

terms.name: Tab stop
terms.definition: One position in the tab sequence: a place the Tab key can reach, counted once even when the widget it belongs to holds many focusable parts.

terms.name: Text spacing
terms.definition: The requirement that a reader can increase line height, letter spacing, word spacing, and paragraph spacing without any content being lost or clipped.

terms.name: Toggle button
terms.definition: A button that stays pressed, reporting an on or off state through aria-pressed rather than firing and returning.

terms.name: Triadic color scheme
terms.definition: A palette of three hues spaced evenly around the colour wheel, vivid by construction and usually applied with one hue dominant.

terms.name: Unsaved changes guard
terms.definition: Warning the reader that edits will be lost before a navigation or close is allowed to proceed, and offering to save or discard first.

terms.name: Vignette
terms.definition: A gradual darkening toward the edges of an image that pulls the eye to the centre, borrowed from lens falloff and applied deliberately for focus and mood.

terms.name: Wireframe
terms.definition: A screen drawn as structure only: blocks where the content goes, a crossed box for an image, ruled lines for text, with no colour or type decided yet.
